Take-home Exercise 3

Station choice as Singapore’s rail network expands

Published

6 November 2026

Modified

7 November 2026

This study uses LTA’s September 2026 train trips to ask how the Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line Phase 1 might change the stations chosen by existing rail users. The proposed network adds 29 distinct station locations. The ridership comparison holds today’s origin trips fixed, so it describes a redistribution under stated assumptions rather than total future demand.

Project outputs

Technical report

Data checks, station geography, model calibration, validation, scenario results, sensitivity, limitations and sources.

Executive summary

Ten content slides with the main maps, charts and cautions for interpreting the estimates.

GitHub project

Quarto source, R scripts, aggregate results, figures and reproduction instructions. The LTA account key and raw trip ZIPs are excluded.

Scope and findings

The Exercise 3 brief asks for current and proposed interaction tables, observed station ridership, a fitted choice model and a market-area comparison. This is one Exercise 3 submission. The station list includes the three Circle Line Stage 6 stations opened in July 2026, giving 184 current physical station locations. The brief’s 24 JRL and 12 CRL1 codes add 29 new locations after existing interchanges are reconciled.

Among 13,436 completed HDB blocks, 9,676 have centroids within 800 m of a current station. The proposed stations bring another 1,319 blocks inside that straight-line threshold. This is a building proximity screen; it does not count residents or actual walking routes.

The September 2026 LTA OD extract supplies 66.78 million weekday trips after excluding 238 same-station trips. All recorded station codes match the updated station list. A separate LTA station-volume file reports 67.42 million weekday tap-outs; the OD destination sum is 99.05% of that figure. I use the OD totals without scaling away the discrepancy.

The fitted model assigns 7.55 million of the fixed current-origin trips to proposed destinations. That is a calculation under the model, not a reliable opening-year forecast. Its in-sample station error averages 193,826 trips and its station-level R² is 0.38. A tougher holdout of Keppel, Cantonment and Prince Edward Road, which opened in July 2026, overpredicts their September tap-outs by 8–159 times. Seven existing interchanges gain trips only when the model gives their added line an attraction uplift; without that uplift, they lose share. The technical report shows these checks and the origin-market map beside the station rankings.

Reproduce the analysis

The README records data sources, exact commands and checksums. The preparation script downloads public HDB, land-use and bus-stop layers. LTA’s monthly trip extracts require an account key and are kept in the excluded private-data folder; the published repository holds only derived aggregate results.
